Paleoclimate: simulations and reconstructions of past climates

Climatologies of past climates from the PMIP model intercomparisons, CLIMBER-3α and CLIMBER-X (stadial and interstadial climates, with the transient output of their simulation), and gridded reconstructions of the deglacial climate of Greenland, remapped onto the grids of the domains. Paleoclimate is a thematic dataset made by remapping (see Gridded data): its products are defined in Paleoclimate/remap.toml.

Products

Product Source Fields Domains
Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<model>-<experiment> PMIP3/CMIP5 (Braconnot et al., 2012, doi:10.1038/nclimate1456): climatologies of the last 100 years of the CMIP5 monthly output (../PMIP3_cmip5/README.md), 13 models: lgm (8: CCSM4, CNRM-CM5, FGOALS-g2, GISS-E2-R, IPSL-CM5A-LR, MIROC-ESM, MPI-ESM-P, MRI-CGCM3), midHolocene and piControl (13, also bcc-csm1-1, CSIRO-Mk3-6-0, FGOALS-s2, HadGEM2-CC, HadGEM2-ES) t2m_ann, t2m_djf, t2m_jja, t2m_mon (degC), pr_ann, pr_djf, pr_jja, pr_mon (mm d-1); z_srf (m), f_land, f_ice of the model and experiment (CMIP5 fixed fields, where published) Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global
Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<model>-<experiment> PMIP4/CMIP6 (Kageyama et al., 2018, doi:10.5194/gmd-11-1033-2018): climatologies of the last 100 years (../PMIP4_cmip6/README.md), 21 models: lgm (7: AWI-ESM-1-1-LR, CESM2-FV2, CESM2-WACCM-FV2, INM-CM4-8, MIROC-ES2L, MPI-ESM1-2-LR, and CESM2-PaleoCalibr of Zhu et al., 2022, ../Zhu2022_PaleoCalibr/README.md), midHolocene (18) and piControl (21) t2m_*, pr_* (annual, DJF, JJA, monthly), z_srf, f_land, f_ice (where published; no pr in CESM2-FV2 lgm) Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global
Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<model>-<experiment>-ocean, Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<model>-<experiment>-ocean The ocean and sea ice of the same runs, where published, from their 1° files (*_ocean.nc of the sources) sst_mon (degC), sic_mon (sea-ice concentration), siext_mon (1 where sic_mon >= 0.15), to_ann (annual potential temperature, degC, at depth 5 to 2000 m), each with its f_valid_<field>; siextent_nh, siextent_sh (hemispheric sea-ice extent, 1e6 km2, as published) Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global
Paleoclimate-PMIP3-<experiment>-mean, -stdev, Paleoclimate-PMIP4-<experiment>-mean, -stdev, and -ocean-mean, -ocean-stdev Ensemble mean and standard deviation of the PMIP3 and of the PMIP4 models of each experiment (PMIP4 lgm without CESM2-FV2, the PaleoCalibr LGM run as published on ESGF, without pr) as the models, with n_<field>, the number of models with a value as above
Paleoclimate-PMIP-lgm-mean, Paleoclimate-PMIP-lgm-stdev Ensemble of 12 LGM runs of PMIP3 and PMIP4: CCSM4, FGOALS-g2, GISS-E2-R, IPSL-CM5A-LR, MIROC-ESM, MPI-ESM-P, MRI-CGCM3, AWI-ESM-1-1-LR, CESM2-PaleoCalibr, INM-CM4-8, MIROC-ES2L, MPI-ESM1-2-LR (not CNRM-CM5, whose LGM run has no ice surface, nor the CESM2-FV2 runs); the reference of the LGM bias correction of the PaleoEmulator climate in kryos as the models, with n_<field> as above
Paleoclimate-PMIP3-lgm-boundary-conditions PMIP3 LGM boundary conditions (Abe-Ouchi et al., 2015, doi:10.5194/gmd-8-3621-2015) dz_srf (m), f_land, f_ice as above
Paleoclimate-CLIMBER3a-<simulation>, Paleoclimate-CLIMBER3a-<simulation>-ocean CLIMBER-3α (Montoya and Levermann, 2008, doi:10.1029/2007GL032560): present day (present) and LGM with wind stress x 1.7, weak and strong Atlantic overturning (lgm_1p7weak, lgm_1p7strong); atmosphere at 22.5° x 7.5°, ocean at 3.75° atmosphere: t2m_ann, t2m_jja (degC), pr_ann (mm d-1), z_srf (m), f_land of the model; ocean: to (potential temperature, degC) on depth, mask_ocn Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global
Paleoclimate-CLIMBERX-Willeit2025-<state>, Paleoclimate-CLIMBERX-Willeit2025-<state>-ocean CLIMBER-X (Willeit et al., 2025, doi:10.1038/s41561-025-01814-0), 5°: climate states of the reference simulation under mid-glacial (MIS3) conditions, interstadial, stadial and heinrich (Heinrich stadial), means of the model years of each state (classified by the Atlantic overturning, see ../Willeit2025_climberx/README.md), and the preindustrial control piControl t2m_*, sst_* (degC), pr_* (mm d-1), f_sic_*, monthly (_mon) and annual (_ann), with their anomalies relative to piControl (*_anom), z_srf, f_land, f_ice of the model; ocean: to (degC), so (psu) on depth, with to_anom, so_anom, mask_ocn Antarctica, GreenlandPaleo, Greenland, North, Laurentide, Eurasia, Global
Paleoclimate-CLIMBERX-Willeit2025-<run>-transient, ...-<run>-transient-ocean The same simulations, HS4 (40-32 ka of the model calendar) and piControl: their 2D output (one model year every 100 years, every 1000 years for piControl), on the model grid t2m_mon, pr_mon, sst_mon, f_sic_mon on month and time, state of each record; annual series on time_ann (amoc, t2m_glob, t2m_grl, co2, hosing, sic_ext_nh, …); ocean: to, so on depth and time, the Atlantic overturning streamfunction moc_atl Global (GLOBAL-5DEG only)
Paleoclimate-Buizert2018, Paleoclimate-Buizert2018-1981-2010 Buizert et al. (2018): Greenland monthly temperature and precipitation, 22 ka to present, decadal, doi:10.25921/psvs-yg80; and its 1981-2010 baseline tas (K), pr (kg m-2 s-1) on month and time (years ago), z_srf Greenland
Paleoclimate-Badgeley2020 Badgeley et al. (2020): Greenland temperature and precipitation from data assimilation, 20 ka to present, 50-year means, doi:10.18739/A2599Z26M tas_anom (K), pr_frac, pr_frac_low, pr_frac_high (relative to 1850-2000 CE) on time (years ago) Greenland

On the mountain-glacier domains (Pyrenees, Patagonia, Himalaya), on their 2 km grid: the atmosphere ensemble means and standard deviations of PMIP3, PMIP4 and PMIP-lgm (-mean, -stdev; not the members or the ocean); their nests and crops get these by cropping (see Nests and crops).

On PatagoniaPaleo (the paleo domain of Patagonia, 26-57°S, 2-8 km), the products of GreenlandPaleo (PMIP3 and PMIP4 members and ensembles, the PMIP3 boundary conditions, CLIMBER-3α and CLIMBER-X), on its coarsest grid, PAT-PAL-8KM.

The model output is on the models’ own grids (some Gaussian), remapped conservatively. Products are made on grids of 8 km and coarser (16 km for the Buizert et al. time series, 32 km for CLIMBER-3α and CLIMBER-X, which are also on global grids of 1° and coarser): finer grids add no information to these sources, and models can remap them online. Each file also has f_valid, the fraction of each cell covered by the source. The ensemble products are made from the files of the models on each grid: in each cell, the mean or the standard deviation (population) of the models with a value there (e.g. sst_mon only over the ocean of each model), n_<field> models.

Precision

The float fields are rounded on output to a tolerance by kind (see Precision and file sizes): temperatures to 0.01 K; precipitation to 1%; z_srf and dz_srf to 0.01 m; fractions (f_*, pr_frac*) to 0.001. The ensemble products are computed from the rounded products of their members and rounded again.

Source Licence

Not included

Large model output, such as the transient TraCE-21ka simulation, is not remapped here: models should read it with online remapping.

Making the dataset

julia -t 8 fesmdata.jl remap Paleoclimate

Downloads

Download the files with fesmdata.jl into $FESMDATA/<Domain>/<GRID>/ (see Download), or one by one from the links below. All released datasets are listed under Products.

Global

Version 2.8.0 (2026-11-13, packages). 797 files, 1.67 GB.

julia fesmdata.jl fetch Paleoclimate Global     # all grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Paleoclimate GLOBAL-5DEG     # one grid
